entities.summary:
Lacydes of Cyrene, Academic Skeptic philosopher, was head of the Platonic Academy at Athens in succession to Arcesilaus from 241 BC. He was forced to resign c. 215 BC due to ill-health, and he died c. 205 BC. Nothing survives of his works.

Lacydes was a prominent figure in the Hellenistic period, succeeding Arcesilaus as the head of the Platonic Academy, and his resignation due to ill-health highlights the challenges faced by scholars during this time.

The Platonic Academy played a significant role in the transmission of Platonic philosophy, and Lacydes' leadership was crucial in shaping the Academy's teachings and influence.

Lacydes' legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as the Platonic Academy continued to thrive after his death, influencing various schools of thought and contributing to the development of Western philosophy.

The fact that nothing survives of his works serves as a poignant reminder of the fragility of intellectual output and the importance of preserving historical records.

The influence of Lacydes can be seen in the works of later philosophers, such as Epictetus, who built upon the foundations laid by Lacydes and the Platonic Academy.

Lacydes' story serves as a testament to the enduring power of ideas and the impact of individual scholars on the course of history.

The Hellenistic period, in which Lacydes lived, was marked by significant cultural, scientific, and philosophical developments, including the rise of the Stoic and Epicurean schools, which were heavily influenced by Platonic thought.

The Platonic Academy's presence in Athens during this time period underscores the city's status as a hub of intellectual inquiry and cultural exchange.

The legacy of Lacydes of Cyrene serves as a reminder of the importance of preserving historical records and the need for continued scholarship and research into the lives and works of influential figures from the past.
